newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cambodia's exiled Prince Sirivudh to fly home.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's exiled Prince Sirivudh to fly home.

text.p: Cambodia's exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh, accused of plotting to kill co-premier Hun Sen, will return to his homeland on Tuesday, his supporters said on Monday.
Prince Sirivudh, half-brother of ruling King Norodom Sihanouk, was sent into exile in December 1995 after being held for one month on charges of alleged involvement in the plot.
He has said he planned to return home for the Cambodian New Year with or without a royal amnesty.
The announcement, released by the prince's support group in Paris, came after a royalist military officer said last week that Sirivudh had decided to put off plans to return.
Hun Sen has warned that violence could erupt between his Cambodian People's Party and the royalist FUNCINPEC party if the prince came home.

The two parties formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run general elections in 1993 and tensions have been high since a deadly grenade attack on a recent demonstration held by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally Sam Rainsy.
Both the prince's half-brother, King Norodom Sihanouk, and First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh have also warned Sirivudh not to return.
